title: Block card set and stage grid
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming sequences and online safety
source: Seeded from computing/y3 lesson 2 (Block card set and stage grid (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 2: Scratch: sprites and motion blocks. To understand how motion blocks in Scratch make a sprite move in sequence

questions.q: Build: when green flag clicked, move 100 steps. What happens?
questions.a: The sprite moves 100 steps in the way it faces.
questions.model: Teacher drags 'when green flag clicked', then snaps 'move 100 steps' under it, predicts 'right 100', then runs it.

questions.q: Change it so the sprite moves back to where it started.
questions.a: Add 'move -100 steps' or turn 180 degrees and move 100 steps.

questions.q: What does 'go to x: 0 y: 0' do?
questions.a: Sends the sprite to the centre of the stage.

questions.q: Core: Make your sprite move in an L shape: move, turn right 90, move.
questions.a: move 100 steps, turn right 90 degrees, move 50 steps.
questions.model: Teacher builds the first part and predicts aloud before clicking the flag.

questions.q: Extend: Make the sprite trace a square and return to the start.
Stretch: Write your script on paper first, predict the end point, then test. Was your prediction right?
questions.a: A written script with a prediction and the result compared.

questions.q: The objects we program in Scratch are called... A) stages B) sprites C) scripts
Why do we predict before we run a script?
questions.a: To check our thinking and spot bugs before testing.
